questions.question: Nasir's birthday is on Thursday 18th May. On what day of the week will be Rehan's Birthday in the same year if Rehan was born on 19th August?
questions.questionHtml: Nasir's birthday is on Thursday 18th May. On what day of the week will be Rehan's Birthday in the same year if Rehan was born on 19th August?
questions.solution:
Nasir’s birthday → 18 May, Thursday

Rehan’s birthday → 19 August

So, May has remaining → 13 Days

June → 30 Days

July → 31 Days

August → 19 Days

Total Days → 93 Days

Dividing 93 days by 7 (as there are 7 days in a week)

We get remainder 2

Thus, 2 days ahead of Nasir’s birthday will be Saturday which is Rehan’s birthday.

Hence, the answer is Saturday.

questions.question: The weights of 4 boxes are 30, 40, 50 and 100 kilograms. Which of the following cannot be the total weight, in kilograms, of any combination of these boxes and in a combination a box can be used only once?
questions.questionHtml: The weights of 4 boxes are 30, 40, 50 and 100 kilograms. Which of the following cannot be the total weight, in kilograms, of any combination of these boxes and in a combination a box can be used only once?
questions.solution:
The possible combinations are:

100 + 50 + 40 = 190

30 + 50 + 100 = 180

100 + 40 = 140                             

But combination for 160 is not possible.

Hence, the answer is 160.

questions.question: In the question, a statement is given, followed by two arguments, I and II. You have to consider the statement to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given arguments, if any, is a strong argument. Statement : Should one year of army training be compulsory for all Indian citizens? Argument I : No, the costs of training will be prohibitive and one year of labour will be lost. Argument II : Yes, army training helps make better citizens.
questions.questionHtml:
In the question, a statement is given, followed by two arguments, I and II. You have to consider the statement to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given arguments, if any, is a strong argument.

Statement: Should one year of army training be compulsory for all Indian citizens?

Argument I: No, the costs of training will be prohibitive and one year of labour will be lost.

Argument II: Yes, army training helps make better citizens.

options.text: If only argument I is strong.
options.html: If only argument I is strong.

options.text: If only argument II is strong.
options.html: If only argument II is strong.

options.text: If both I and II are strong.
options.html: If both I and II are strong.

options.text: If neither I nor II is strong.
options.html: If neither I nor II is strong.

questions.solution:
Statement: Should one year of army training be compulsory for all Indian citizens?

Argument I: No, the costs of training will be prohibitive and one year of labour will be lost. → Due to the training, there will be a loss of labour for one year. Therefore argument I is strong.

Argument II: Yes, army training helps make better citizens. → Clearly, it is not necessary that the army training helps to make a better citizen. The impact of training differs from person to person. So, the argument II is vague.

Hence, the only argument I is strong.

Important Points In question of Statement and Arguments, it is not necessary that statement contains all the things which are given in arguments. In these questions, we just have to think that whether the arguments are strong or not.

questions.question: "Relief of the disabled and unemployable" is listed in the __________ list given in the Seventh Schedule in the Constitution of India.
questions.questionHtml: "Relief of the disabled and unemployable" is listed in the __________ list given in the Seventh Schedule in the Constitution of India.
questions.solution:
Option 2 is correct, i.e. State.

  • The state list or List-II is a list of 61 items in Schedule Seven to the constitution of India.
  • Initially, there were 66 items in the list.
  •  "Relief of the disabled and unemployable" is listed in the state list.

Extra facts:

Seventh Schedule of the Indian constitution gives allocation of powers and functions between Union & States. It contains 3 lists:-

1. Union List (For central Govt) 100 Subjects (originally 97).

2. States List (Powers of State Govt) 61 subjects  (originally 66). 

3.Concurrent List (Both Union & States) 52 subjects (originally 47).

questions.question: ________ amends the Constitution.
questions.questionHtml: ________ amends the Constitution.

options.text: Securities and Exchange Board of India
options.html: Securities and Exchange Board of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Parliament.

Key Points

  • Amending the Constitution of India is the process of making changes to the nation's fundamental law or supreme law.
  • The procedure of amendment in the constitution is laid down in Part XX (Article 368) of the Constitution of India.
  • This procedure ensures the sanctity of the Constitution of India and keeps a check on the arbitrary power of the Parliament of India.

Additional Information

  • The Parliament can amend the constitution in three ways:
    • By simple majority.
    • By special majority.
    • By special majority but with the consent of half of all the state legislature.
  • By simple majority:  A simple majority, that is, a majority of the members of the House present and voting. 
  • By special majority:  A special majority of the Parliament, i.e., a two-third majority of the members of each House present and voting, and a majority (that is, more than 50 percent), of the total membership of each House. 
  • By special majority but with the concern of half of all the state legislature.

questions.question: In each testes in a male reproductive system, there are ________ compartments called testicular lobules.
questions.questionHtml: In each testes in a male reproductive system, there are ________ compartments called testicular lobules.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 250.

Explanation: The glandular structure of the testis consists of numerous lobules. Their number, in a single testis, is estimated by Berres at 250.

Functions:

  • The testicles are the male gonads — the primary male reproductive organs. They have two, very important functions that are very important to the male reproductive system: they produce gametes or sperm, and they secrete hormones, primarily testosterone. 
  • Each testicle consists of a series of small tubes, or tubules, that contain testosterone and sperm-producing cells.
  • Seminiferous tubules house germ cells — the 23 chromosome cells that men replicate to produce sperm and they are the site of sperm production, or spermatogenesis, according to VMC.
  • These tubules are tightly coiled within the testis, and each testis may contain up to 900 tubules. The tubules are almost 20 inches (50 cm) long, and a typical testis contains up to half a mile (800 meters) of seminiferous tubules.

questions.question: The predominant stage of the life cycle of a moss is the gametophyte which consists of two stages. The second stage is the _________ stage.
questions.questionHtml: The predominant stage of the life cycle of a moss is the gametophyte which consists of two stages. The second stage is the _________ stage.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Leafy

Explanation:

In the life cycle of mosses, the gametophyte stage includes two main stages:

  • Protonema: The first stage, which is a thread-like structure that develops from the spore.
  • Leafy: The second stage, which develops from the protonema and consists of a small leafy plant. The leafy stage develops from a lateral bud in the secondary protonema. It is a small leafy structure consisting of rhizoids, leaves and stem. It bears sex organs antheridia and archegonia.

questions.question: In Animal Kingdom classification, which of the following is not a Phylum?
questions.questionHtml: In Animal Kingdom classification, which of the following is not a Phylum?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Coelomates.

Key Points

  • The animals which possess true coelom are called eucoelomates or coelomates. The true coelom is a body cavity which arises as a cavity in embryonic mesoderm.
  • In more simpler words, any animal possessing a fluid-filled cavity within which the digestive system is suspended is called coelomates.

Additional Information

  • Living organisms are classified into five kingdoms.
    • ​Kingdom Monera.
    • Kingdom Protista.
    • Kingdom Fungi.
    • Kingdom Plante.
    • Kingdom Animalia. 

Important Points

  • Further classification is done by the following scheme: Kingdom, Phylum (for animals) / Division (for plants), Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.

questions.question: _________ is the interaction in which one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited.
questions.questionHtml: _________ is the interaction in which one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Commensalism.

Key Points

  • The species that gains the benefit is called the commensal.
  • The other species is called the host species.
  • Example- A golden jackal (the commensal) following a tiger (the host ) to feed on leftovers from its kills. 

Additional Information

  • Predation is the ecological process by which energy is transferred from living animals to living animals based on the behavior of a predator that captures and kills prey before eating it.
  • Competition is an interaction between organisms or species in which both the organisms or species are harmed.
  • Parasitism is the relationship between two species of plants or animals in which one benefits at the expense of the other, sometimes without killing the host organism.

questions.question: Select the correct option: Convert binary 10110 to decimal.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct option:

Convert binary 10110 to decimal.
questions.solution:
A binary number is converted to decimal by multiplying each binary digit by 2n, where ‘n’ is the place of the digit, such as 0, 1, 2,…

∴ (10110)2 = (1 × 24) + (0 × 23) + (1 × 22) + (1 × 21) + (0 × 20) = 16 + 4 + 2 = 22

questions.question: A, B and C can do a job working alone in 12, 16 and 24 days respectively. In how many days they can do the job if they worked together?
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C can do a job working alone in 12, 16 and 24 days respectively. In how many days they can do the job if they worked together?
questions.solution:
Formula used:

Total Work = Efficiency × Total Time

Calculation:

Let the total work be 48 units (LCM of 12, 16 and 24)

⇒ Efficiency of A = 48/12 = 4 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of B = 48/16 = 3 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of C = 48/24 = 2 units/day

Combined efficiency of A, B and C = 4 + 3 + 2 = 9 units/day

⇒ Total time required = 48/9 = 16/3 days

∴ While working together, A, B and C will complete the work in 16/3 days.

questions.question: If on a Sale there is 40% discount on the marked price of Rs. 1000, but the sale is done at Rs. 510 only then what additional discount (in %) did the customer get?
questions.questionHtml: If on a Sale there is 40% discount on the marked price of Rs. 1000, but the sale is done at Rs. 510 only then what additional discount (in %) did the customer get?
questions.solution:
Let the additional successive discount be ‘d%’

Marked price = Rs. 1000

Selling price = Rs. 510

First discount = 40%

∵ Selling price = Marked price – discount price

⇒ 510 = (100 – d)% of (100 – 40)% of 1000

⇒ 510 = (100 – d)/100 × 0.6 × 1000

⇒ 510 = 600 – 6d

⇒ 6d = 90

⇒ d = 90/6 = 15%

∴ The additional discount is 15%

questions.question: In a class of 39 students, there are 26 girls. The average weight of these girls is 42 Kgs and the average weight of the full class is 48 kgs. What is the average weight (in kgs) of the boys in the class?
questions.questionHtml: In a class of 39 students, there are 26 girls. The average weight of these girls is 42 Kgs and the average weight of the full class is 48 kgs. What is the average weight (in kgs) of the boys in the class?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Number of Boys = 39 − 26 = 13. Ratio of Girls : Boys = 26 : 13 = 2 : 1.

Deviation of Girls average (42) from Class average (48) = −6.

Total deviation for 2 units of girls = 2 × (−6) = −12.

To balance, deviation for 1 unit of boys must be +12.

Average weight of boys = 48 + 12 = 60 kg.

∴ The correct answer is 60 kg.

Alternate Method

Given: Total students = 39, Girls = 26, Avg weight of girls = 42 kg, Avg weight of class = 48 kg.

Formula: Total Weight = Average × Number of students

⇒ Number of Boys = 39 − 26 = 13

⇒ Total weight of the class = 39 × 48 = 1872 kg

⇒ Total weight of girls = 26 × 42 = 1092 kg

⇒ Total weight of boys = 1872 − 1092 = 780 kg

⇒ Average weight of boys = 780 ÷ 13

⇒ Average weight of boys = 60 kg

∴ The correct answer is 60 kg.

Additional Information

Weighted Average Formula

The combined average of two groups is given by Aavg = (n1w1 + n2w2) ÷ (n1 + n2), where n is the count and w is the weight.

Deviation Method

The sum of deviations of all observations from the mean is always zero. This helps in finding missing values quickly without large multiplications.

Rule of Alligation

(Quantity of Cheaper) ÷ (Quantity of Dearer) = (Rate of Dearer − Mean Rate) ÷ (Mean Rate − Rate of Cheaper).

questions.question: If a saree is sold for Rs. 2880 the seller will face 10% loss, at what price (in Rs) should he sell to gain 20% profit?
questions.questionHtml: If a saree is sold for Rs. 2880 the seller will face 10% loss, at what price (in Rs) should he sell to gain 20% profit?
questions.solution:
When selling price = Rs. 2880, loss = 10%

∵ Cost price – loss = Selling price

⇒ CP – 10% of CP = 2880

⇒ 0.9CP = 2880

⇒ Cost price = 2880/0.9 = Rs. 3200

∵ Selling price = Cost price + Profit

∴ To gain a profit of 20%, selling price = 3200 + 20% × 3200 = Rs. 3840

questions.question: Priya got 9 marks more in History than what she got in Geography. Her history marks are 56% of the sum of her History and Geography marks. What are her Geography marks?
questions.questionHtml: Priya got 9 marks more in History than what she got in Geography. Her history marks are 56% of the sum of her History and Geography marks. What are her Geography marks?
questions.solution:
Let Priya’s marks in Geography and History be ‘x’ and ‘y’ respectively

She got 9 more marks in History than in Geography,

⇒ y = x + 9

Also, her History marks is 56% of sum of both marks

⇒ y = 56% of (x + y)

⇒ y = 0.56x + 0.56y

⇒ 0.44y = 0.56x

Substituting for y,

⇒ 0.44(x + 9) = 0.56x

⇒ 0.44x + 3.96 = 0.56x

⇒ 0.12x = 3.96

⇒ x = 3.96/0.12 = 33

∴ Priya’s Geography marks = 33

questions.question: To travel 720 km, a Express train takes 6 hours more than Duronto. If however, the speed of the Express train is doubled, it takes 2 hours less than Duronto. The speed of Duronto (in km/hr) is?
questions.questionHtml: To travel 720 km, a Express train takes 6 hours more than Duronto. If however, the speed of the Express train is doubled, it takes 2 hours less than Duronto. The speed of Duronto (in km/hr) is?
questions.solution:
Let the speed of Duronto be ‘x’ km/hr

Time taken by Duronto to travel 720 km = 720/x hrs.

Let the initial speed of Express train be ‘y’ km/hr

Time taken by Express train to travel 720 km = 720/y hrs.

∵ Express train takes 6 hours more than Duronto,

⇒ 720/y = 6 + 720/x      ----(1)

When the speed of Express train is doubled, it takes 2 hours less than Duronto,

⇒ 720/2y = 720/x – 2

⇒ 720/y = 1440/x – 4

Substituting from (1),

⇒ 6 + 720/x = 1440/x – 4

⇒ 6 + 4 = 1440/x – 720/x

⇒ 10 = 720/x

⇒ x = 720/10 = 72 km/hr

∴ Speed of Duronto = 72 km/hr

questions.question: What is the difference (in Rs) between the compound interests on Rs. 1000 for 1 year at 10% per annum compounded yearly and half-yearly?
questions.questionHtml: What is the difference (in Rs) between the compound interests on Rs. 1000 for 1 year at 10% per annum compounded yearly and half-yearly?
questions.solution:
GIVEN:

P = Rs. 1000

Rate = 10%

Time = 1 year

FORMULA USED:

On a sum of Rs. P at rate of R% per annum after n years,

Compound interest = P[(1 + R/100)n – 1], when compounded annually

Compound interest = P[(1 + R/200)2n – 1], when compounded half-yearly

CALCULATION:

Interest compounded annually = 1000 × (1 + 10/100 – 1) = 1000 × 0.1 = Rs. 100

Interest compounded half-yearly = 1000 × [(1 + 10/200)2 – 1] = 1000 × 0.1025 = Rs. 102.5

∴ Required difference = 102.5 – 100 = Rs. 2.5

questions.question: If 7x - (3/2) × (4x - 9) = 6.5, then the value of x is?

∴ The correct answer is option (3).

questions.question: The sum of a non-zero number and 4 times its reciprocal is 17/2. What is the number?
questions.questionHtml: The sum of a non-zero number and 4 times its reciprocal is 17/2. What is the number?
questions.solution:
Let the number be ‘x’

⇒ x + 4/x = 17/2

⇒ 2x2 + 8 = 17x

⇒ 2x2 – 17x + 8 = 0

⇒ 2x2 – 16x – x + 8 = 0

⇒ 2x(x – 8) – 1(x – 8) = 0

⇒ (x – 8)(2x – 1) = 0

⇒ x = 8, 1/2

∴ The number is 8

questions.question: The 5th and 9th term of an arithmetic progression are 7 and 13 respectively. What is the 15th term?
questions.questionHtml: The 5th and 9th term of an arithmetic progression are 7 and 13 respectively. What is the 15th term?
questions.solution:
The nth term of an AP with first term ‘a’ and difference ‘d’ = a + (n – 1)d

5th term = a + 4d = 7     ----(1)

9th term = a + 8d = 13     ----(2)

Subtracting (1) from (2), we get,

⇒ a + 8d – a – 4d = 13 – 7

⇒ 4d = 6

⇒ d = 3/2

Substituting in (1),

⇒ a = 7 – 4(3/2) = 1

∴ 15th term = a + 14d = 1 + 14(3/2) = 1 + 21 = 22

questions.question: What is the reflection of the point (6, -3) in the line y = 2?
questions.questionHtml: What is the reflection of the point (6, -3) in the line y = 2?
questions.solution:
When a point is reflected about the x-axis, the x-coordinate remains the same and only the y-coordinate is transformed

  

∵ The line y = 2 is parallel to the x-axis, x-coordinate will remain the same after reflection

Now, along the y-direction, the distance between the reflected point and the line will be equal to the distance between the original point and the line

⇒ Distance between point and line along y-direction = |-3 – (2)| = |-5| = 5 unit

⇒ Y-coordinate of reflection = 2 + 5 = 7

∴ The reflection point is (6, 7)

questions.question: Point A (24/7, 2) divides segment BC in the ratio 2 : 5. Co-ordinates of B are (2, 6) and C are (7, y). What is the value of y?
questions.questionHtml: Point A (24/7, 2) divides segment BC in the ratio 2 : 5. Co-ordinates of B are (2, 6) and C are (7, y). What is the value of y?
questions.solution:
Given:

A (24/7, 2) divides segment BC in the ratio 2 : 5

Solution:

According to the section formula,

⇒ If a point A(x, y) that lies on a line segment BC joining points B(x1, y1) and C(x2, y2), divides the line in the ratio m∶ n, then the coordinates of A can be computed as,

⇒ Coordinates of A = (x, y) = [(mx2 + nx1)/(m + n)], [(my2 + ny1)/(m + n)]

Given, point A(24/7, 2) divides the segment joining B(2, 6) and C(7, y) in the ratio 2 ∶ 5,

Hence,

Coordinates of A = (24/7, 2) = [(7m + 2n)/(m + n)], [(y m + 6n)/(m + n)]

Considering y-coordinate,

⇒ 2 = (y m + 6n)/(m + n)

Substituting for m and n,

⇒ 2 = (2y + 30)/7

⇒ 14 = 2y + 30

⇒ 2y = -16

∴ y = -8

questions.question: At what point does the line 2x - 3y = 6 cuts the X axis?
questions.questionHtml: At what point does the line 2x - 3y = 6 cuts the X axis?
questions.solution:
Given:

⇒ 2x - 3y = 6 

Solution:

We know that,

At x – axis, the value of y-coordinate is zero

Putting y = 0,

⇒ 2x - 3y = 6

⇒ 2x - 3(0) = 6

⇒ 2x = 6

⇒ x = 6/2 = 3

∴ The required point is (3, 0)

questions.question: ∆ABC is right angled at B. BD is an altitude. AD = 4 cm and DC = 9 cm. What is the value of BD (in cm)?
questions.questionHtml: ∆ABC is right angled at B. BD is an altitude. AD = 4 cm and DC = 9 cm. What is the value of BD (in cm)?
questions.solution:
Let the length of BD be ‘x’ cm

In the given figure below,

Applying Pythagoras theorem in ∆ABD,

⇒ AB2 = AD2 + BD2 = x2 + 16

Applying Pythagoras theorem in ∆BCD,

⇒ BC2 = BD2 + CD2 = x2 + 81

Applying Pythagoras theorem in ∆ABC,

⇒ AC2 = AB2 + BC2

⇒ (4 + 9)2 = x2 + 16 + x2 + 81

⇒ 2x2 = 72

⇒ x2 = 36

⇒ x = √36 = 6 cm

∴ Value of BD = 6 cm

questions.question: ΔXYZ is right angled at Y. If ∠Z = 60°, then Cosec X =
questions.questionHtml: ΔXYZ is right angled at Y. If ∠Z = 60°, then Cosec X =

⇒ ∠X = 180° – 150° = 30°

⇒  cosec 30° = 2

questions.question: If Cosec θ = 17/8, then Cot θ = ?
questions.questionHtml: If Cosec θ = 17/8, then Cot θ = ?
questions.solution:
Given:

Cosec θ = 17/8

Solution:

Using trigonometric identities,

⇒ cosec2 θ = 1 + cot2 θ

⇒ cot2 θ = cosec2 θ – 1

⇒  289/64 – 1

 ⇒ cot2 θ  = 225/64

∴  cot2 θ  = √(225/64)

 ⇒ cot2 θ = 15/8

questions.question: In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given. Fossilize
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.

Fossilize
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Amalgamate.

Key Points

  • The word "Fossilize" means to become a fossil or to make something become a fossil; it can also imply becoming outdated or rigid in thinking. (जीवाश्म बनाना)
    • Example: Over time, the bones fossilized and were preserved in the rock.
  • "Amalgamate" means to combine or unite to form one organization or structure. (विलय करना)
    • Example: The two companies decided to amalgamate to increase their market share.
  • Hence, we can infer that the word similar in meaning to 'Fossilize' is 'Amalgamate'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Amalgamate.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Dissolve (घुलना): To make a solid become part of a liquid.
    • Example: Sugar dissolves easily in hot water.
  • Flex (मोड़ना): To bend or move something, especially a muscle.
    • Example: He flexed his muscles to show off his strength.
  • Liquefy (तरल बनाना): To make or become liquid.
    • Example: The heat liquefied the chocolate.

Z -dry for game, and with the exception

questions.solution:
